title: A shallow clone silently disables STALE_AFTER_BUILDS aging in qa:triage
body:
Found by the 2026-09-02 repository audit while fixing the sibling defect in
scripts/verify-bug-traces.ts (bug_0594). Same root cause, opposite failure mode: the
bug-traces gate failed LOUDLY and wrongly; triage degrades SILENTLY.

## What breaks

`buildHistory()` (bin/triage.ts:53) reads the recency spine with `git log --format=%H`.
That is honest about the commits a checkout HAS, and a shallow clone has almost none. On
a `git clone --depth 1` the spine is exactly ONE commit.

`buildsSince` (src/qa/triage.ts:198) is `buildHistory.indexOf(build)`, returning null when
the build is not found, and the aging rule (src/qa/triage.ts:277) is:

    if (!isVerified && age !== null && age > STALE_AFTER_BUILDS) status = "stale";

So with a one-commit spine every ticket whose `last_seen_build` is not that exact commit
gets `age === null` and is permanently exempt from aging. STALE_AFTER_BUILDS becomes
inert, the bucket reports `stale 0`, and findings that were fixed builds ago keep
presenting as actionable work to the dev loop.

## Why this is the regression the file says it already fixed

The docstring above `buildHistory()` describes this exact failure as history: with the
previous `-n200` window "every session played on a build older than the last two hundred
was permanently exempt from STALE_AFTER_BUILDS, which is precisely the ticket most likely
to describe something already fixed." That fix removed the SELF-INFLICTED window. A
shallow clone reintroduces an identical, tighter window from the environment, and nothing
detects it. AGENTS.md tells agents to rely on this rule ("triage ages findings out after
STALE_AFTER_BUILDS; do not hand-wave past either"), so an agent trusting it in a shallow
checkout is trusting a rule that is not running.

## Reproduction

    git clone --depth 1 file://$PWD /tmp/shallow
    cd /tmp/shallow
    git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository   # true
    git log --format=%H | wc -l             # 1   <- the whole spine

Confirmed against this checkout: depth-1 gives a 1-line spine; `git fetch --unshallow`
restores 1639.

Related and already visible: tests/unit/qa_triage_cli.test.ts:130 fails on a shallow
clone at its own `expect(history.length).toBeGreaterThan(300)` guard. That guard is
working as intended — it is named here only so the next reader recognises the same cause.

## Proposed fix

Probe `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` and say so. The fail-open on null age is
still right (expiring a ticket whose build was never published would be worse), so this
should WARN loudly rather than exit nonzero — triage runs inside the playtest loop and
failing it would stop evidence flowing. Something like:

    ! shallow clone: build history is truncated, so staleness aging is disabled and
      stale tickets will still read as actionable. Run `git fetch --unshallow`.

## Why it was not fixed in the audit's own pass

The 6-line warning is easy; making it PROVABLE is not, and this repo tests its
history-dependent guards by injection rather than by trusting them (see
tests/regression/verify_integrity_fail_closed.test.ts for COUNT_BASELINE_UNREADABLE, and
the `shallowHistory` option bug_0594 added for the same reason). bin/triage.ts calls
`main()` unconditionally at module load, so it cannot be imported by a test; covering the
warning needs either a shared, testable git-history helper under src/ (also used by
scripts/verify-bug-traces.ts, which currently has its own copy of the probe) or a
shallow-clone harness in tests/unit/qa_triage_cli.test.ts. Both are QA/tooling-subsystem
changes beyond the one focused change that pass was making, and the warn-vs-fail choice
is an owner call. Filed rather than guessed.
